newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ hijack alert sparks swoop in US.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ hijack alert sparks swoop in US.

text.p: Armed FBI agents swooped on an Air New Zealand jet at Los Angeles after the pilot wrongly activated a hijack alert just before landing, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Tuesday.

Several agents and airport police officers raced to the plane as it came to a halt on the tarmac. The 747 jet, which was isolated from other air traffic for security reasons after the alert, was delayed for 45 minutes before agents finally gave clearance for the air crew and 281 passengers to disembark.

Superintendent John Hicks, of the Los Angeles airport's operations bureau, said the alert was triggered when the one of the crew activated a hijack signal from the flight deck after a flight from Heathrow Airport, London, last Thursday.
The signal warned air traffic controllers, airport police and FBI staff of the possibility that the plane had been hijacked.

FBI agents then contacted the crew by radio and discovered a mistake had been made. But agents decided to board the plane and interview the crew before permitting the plane to taxi to the main terminal.
Hicks said false hijack alerts were highly unusual.
"I don't think it has happened since I've been here and I've worked here since 1953," he said.
It was unlikely the airport would charge Air New Zealand for the cost of the callout.
Air New Zealand spokesman Cameron Hill was reluctant to give details of the incident because it would reveal how the airline handled security matters.
